en: A Half Day at the Terracotta Army: Excavation Before Formation
zh: 兵马俑半日：先看考古，再看军阵
ja: 兵馬俑を半日で：発掘から軍陣を読む

p.src: Before entering the Pit 1 hall, put the Terracotta Army back into its mausoleum landscape. The First Emperor's burial mound stands to the west; the principal warrior pits lie about 1.5 kilometres east of it. Burials, accompanying pits, roads and building remains extend through the ground between and around them. The ranks seen from the railing are neither the burial chamber nor the whole mausoleum. Establish that spatial relationship first, before pit numbers, troop types and totals take over the visit.

p.src: In March 1974, villagers digging a well at Lintong found fragments of terracotta figures. Investigation identified Pit 1; Pits 2 and 3 were found in 1976. The episode is often compressed into a single lucky strike that revealed an underground army. What followed was half a century of survey, excavation, joining, recording and conservation. In the hall, look beyond the most complete general: trench edges, work areas and seams across reconstructed bodies show that the display is also a record of archaeological decisions.

p.src: The pits were underground earth-and-timber structures. Rammed-earth partitions divided corridors; posts, beams and planking supported a roof covered with reed matting and soil. Figures, horses and chariots stood within those passages. Timber later burned or decayed, and the roof mass collapsed, crushing many figures. Traces of fire are real, but not every break can be assigned to one burning episode. Read the partitions, corridors and collapse layers together instead of picturing an intact army simply lowered into the ground.

p.src: The two panels deliberately use different scales. The left shows only the relationship between the burial mound and the warrior-pit sector; the right compares Pits 1, 2 and 3 at one scale using published dimensions. Pit outlines and relative positions are generalized, so this is neither an excavation survey nor a navigation map. Pit 1 is the broadest, Pit 2 has an irregular L-shaped plan, and Pit 3 is markedly smaller. Use the diagram to establish scale before the exhibition halls turn building size into an apparent measure of the whole mausoleum.

caption.zh: 两个尺度下的秦始皇帝陵示意：左图说明封土与兵马俑坑区的关系，右图按公布尺寸比较一、二、三号坑。坑形和相对位置经过概化，不是考古测绘图。
caption.ja: 二つの縮尺で見る秦始皇帝陵。左図は墳丘と兵馬俑坑地区の関係、右図は公表寸法に基づく一号坑・二号坑・三号坑の比較。坑の形と相対位置は概略化しており、考古測量図ではない。
caption.en: The First Emperor's mausoleum at two scales: mound and warrior-pit sector at left, then Pits 1, 2 and 3 compared from published dimensions. Pit shapes and relative positions are generalized; this is not an excavation survey.

p.src: Pit 1 measures 230 by 62 metres and contains the most extensive formation of the three principal warrior pits. A transverse vanguard stands at the east, with the main body facing east through long corridors and guarding formations along the sides and rear. It is useful to read this as a representation of military order, but not as a snapshot of one day on a battlefield. Figures, chariots, horses and weapons belonged to an imperial funerary programme, and today's view is limited to areas selected for excavation, conservation and display.

caption.zh: 在一号坑东端，第一眼先放在整体：现代大厅的跨度、夯土隔墙与长廊中的俑列同时出现。栏杆只让人看到已经发掘、修复并开放展示的一部分，不是完整陵园。
caption.ja: 一号坑の東端では、まず現代ホールの大きな架構、版築の隔壁、長い通路に並ぶ俑を一つの視野に入れる。手すり越しに見えるのは、発掘・修復され公開された一部であり、陵園全体ではない。
caption.en: At Pit 1's east end, begin with the whole field: the span of the modern hall, rammed-earth partitions and rows of figures in the long corridors. The railing reveals only the excavated, conserved and displayed portion, not the full mausoleum.

p.src: Pit 2 matters not because it contains more figures than Pit 1, but because it combines them differently. Excavators have interpreted several units containing crossbowmen, chariots, infantry and cavalry from their find positions. Much remains unexposed. Bare soil and protective coverings do not mean that nothing is there; excavation proceeds according to research questions and conservation capacity. If Pit 1 offers the broad formation, Pit 2 is where to examine mixed arms and the value of leaving evidence undisturbed.

p.src: Pit 3 covers only about 520 square metres. Its concave plan and scale differ sharply from Pits 1 and 2. The arrangement of a chariot, warriors, weapons and passages has led some scholars to interpret it as a command post or ceremonial space; the museum describes this as a scholarly view rather than a settled fact. The qualification matters. Pit 3 is not a miniature Pit 1. Its value lies in leaving the location and function of the formation's centre open to investigation.

p.src: The figures do not force a choice between 'every face was a portrait' and 'the whole army came from one mould'. Research on ceramic fabrics and working traces suggests that clay was processed relatively centrally and distributed to several workshops near the mausoleum. Repeatable procedures shaped parts such as heads, hands and bodies; assembly, finishing, incised detail and paint introduced further variation. Organized production still left room for differences introduced by hand. Hair, armour plates, folds and ears are best read for that interaction, not used to invent a biography for one face.

p.src: The familiar grey-brown surface is not the figures' original visual state. Lacquer and painted layers have survived on many excavated figures, but they are highly sensitive to moisture loss, changing temperature and humidity, and weakening adhesion; curling, lifting and flaking can follow exposure. Excavating more does not automatically preserve more. The image on this page conveys the working scale of recording, cleaning and joining. It depicts no specific object or real conservation room and cannot substitute for excavation photography or conservation records.

caption.zh: 现代教学复制件上的保护原理演示：残片先被记录、清理和试拼，发掘并不等于工作结束。场景不对应某件文物或真实保护室。
caption.ja: 現代の教材用レプリカで保存工程を学ぶ。破片は記録、クリーニング、仮接合を経る。特定の遺物や実在の保存室を示すものではない。
caption.en: A conservation sequence demonstrated with modern teaching replicas: fragments are recorded, cleaned and trial-fitted. No specific object or real conservation room is depicted.

p.src: Allow at least an unhurried half-day for Lintong. The museum has two visitor areas: the Terracotta Army Museum and Lishan Garden. As checked on 14 August 2026, official guidance recommends about 1.5 hours in each, with a free shuttle and real-name reservation. Add the journey from central Xi'an, queues, security and a meal separately. Visit the pits first, then use Lishan Garden to recover the mausoleum's scale. Hours, tickets, reservations and transport change, so check the museum website or official WeChat before leaving. Chapter 7 covers combinations with Huaqing Palace.
